edits.headline: Iran war toll: at least 21 U.S. troops dead, 860-plus wounded, Task & Purpose reports
edits.summary: Task & Purpose has updated its running timeline of the U.S.-Iran war, which began Feb. 28, 2026. The outlet says fighting has swung between heavy combat and lulls but never fully stopped. It reports at least 21 American service members killed and more than 860 wounded in action. The timeline is still being updated.
edits.take: We'd put the wounded number up front. More than 860 hurt means a lot of troops and families heading into long recoveries, and some will need the VA for years. A "ceasefire in name only" is also the kind of spin we watch closely. Troops are still taking fire whatever the press releases call it. The country owes them clear answers on the mission and care that is ready when they come home.
edits.x_post: Task & Purpose's updated Iran war timeline: the conflict began Feb. 28, 2026. At least 21 U.S. service members are dead and more than 860 wounded in action. The outlet says fighting has never truly stopped, despite a nominal ceasefire.
edits.fb_post:
Task & Purpose has updated its running timeline of the U.S.-Iran war, which began Feb. 28, 2026.

The outlet reports at least 21 American service members killed and more than 860 wounded in action. It says the fighting has moved between open conflict and lulls, and has never truly stopped. A ceasefire existed in name only, with exchanges of fire continuing and Iran striking targets across the region.

Why it matters: those wounded numbers mean many troops and families facing long recoveries and years of VA care. We think the country owes them straight answers about the mission, and care that is ready before they need it.

For those serving or with someone deployed: what information do you wish you were getting more clearly?
edits.why_it_matters: For service members and families, the numbers show this is a sustained conflict with real casualties, not a one-time strike, and the ceasefire label may not match conditions on the ground.
